title: Deref Implementation Exposing Name Collisions
pattern: Defining public inherent methods (like `clone()`) on a type that implements `Deref` to a user-controlled target type.
why_bad: If the underlying target type T also has a method with the same name, calling `pointer.clone()` becomes highly ambiguous or unexpectedly invokes T's method, leading to logic bugs.
detection: A struct implements `Deref` and declares public inherent methods (especially those matching standard trait methods like clone, borrow, etc.).
counterexample: Smart pointer types like `Arc` and `Box` use associated static functions (e.g., `Arc::clone(&my_arc)`) instead of inherent methods.
fix: Expose the method as an associated static function: `pub fn clone(ptr: &Self) -> Self` instead of taking `&self`.
source: Rust For Rustaceans, Chapter 4 (Deref and Inherent Methods) [418].
